claims.text: Bulk W-Ta-Cr-V-based refractory HEAs can maintain useful phase stability under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
Conventionally processed refractory HEAs have relatively coarse-grained microstructures.
Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled low-temperature annealing will produce a stable ultrafine-grained microstructure in bulk refractory HEAs.
The proposed processing route will tailor grain-boundary segregation.
The engineered ultrafine grains and grain-boundary segregation will suppress detrimental phase transformations or precipitate formation.
Severe plastic deformation refines grains in the refractory HEA.
Severe plastic deformation introduces a high dislocation density in the refractory HEA.
Controlled annealing promotes beneficial grain-boundary segregation.
Controlled annealing stabilizes the refined grain structure.
The combined treatment enhances dislocation motion during deformation.
Enhanced dislocation motion from the combined treatment will improve both strength and ductility.
The combined treatment mitigates grain growth at high temperature.
The combined treatment mitigates irradiation-induced defect accumulation.
Relative to conventionally processed material, the treated alloy will exhibit higher yield strength.
Relative to conventionally processed material, the treated alloy will exhibit greater ductility.
The mechanical-property improvements will occur without a significant loss of phase stability.
The treatment will not increase susceptibility to irradiation damage.
W-Ta-Cr-V refractory HEAs can resist irradiation-induced loop formation, helium-bubble growth, and radiation-induced grain-boundary segregation.
Cr- and V-rich precipitates in a W-Ta-Cr-V refractory HEA may be detrimental to mechanical properties through embrittlement.
Small-scale experiments and nanocrystalline thin-film studies support grain refinement as beneficial for refractory HEAs.
